segments.text: DAWN SONG: Thanks, everyone, for being here, really.
Welcome everyone to the second day of our Agentic AI Summit.
We are really excited about the fast advancement in frontier AI.
And also, as Jennifer mentioned, now we're
also seeing that the gap is narrowing between open weights,
models, and proprietary models.
And I want to share a little bit of the history of how
all this got started and how we got here.
So back in 2024--
back then, actually not many people
were talking about agentic AI.
But however, at RDI, we could see
that the agents are the next frontier
and agents are the future.
So in fall of 2024, we launched the world's first course
and the first MOOC-- massive online course on agentic AI.
And then come year 2025, even though I
knew that agents is the next frontier, agents is the future.
But even I was surprised.
Come around year 2025, it suddenly
became the year of agents.
And then we continue to see the fast growth in agentic AI.
And last fall 2025, we launched the first edition
of agentic summit at UC Berkeley.
And then together with the fast growth of agentic AI,
we continue to lead the agentic AI MOOC with over 40,000
enrolled globally.
And also come to this year, we are here
for the second edition of agentic AI summit.
And again, thanks, everyone, for being here.
We are continuing to see the fast growth in agentic AI.
And going forward, we foresee that the growth
will be even further fueled by a number of factors.
We are seeing unprecedented CapEx spending,
and also we are seeing exponential growth
in AI compute capacity.
For example, global AI compute capacity
is doubling every seven months.
And you can see for the hyperscalers,
their CapEx spending is also increasing drastically.
And when we put all the CapEx spending by the hyperscaler
together, it's reaching an unprecedented scale.
It dwarfs all the largest CapEx spending in US history--
the US mega projects.
For example, dwarfs the Manhattan project's,
the Marshall projects, and the Apollo program.
And again, where will this lead us to?
We foresee a further explosive growth of AI agents.
And with that, on one hand, we want
to benefit from the great capabilities and power
of this agentic AI that can bring benefits and prosperity
to all sectors of society.
But on the other hand, we also need
to pay attention to a broad spectrum
of different types of AI risks.
Here's just one example of some of our recent work--
in particular, in the space of cybersecurity.
For example, cybercrime.
Our benchmark-- which has been used by all frontier AI labs--
it's a leading benchmark that helps evaluate frontier AI
capabilities in cybersecurity-- in particular,
for vulnerability discovery, and also for generating Proof
of Concepts--
POCs.
These are inputs that actually triggers the vulnerability.
So when you look at the performance on CyberGym,
it demonstrates the fast increase of frontier AI
capabilities in cybersecurity.
And also, it shows that frontier AI models,
not only they can discover previously known
vulnerabilities, but they can also
discover zero-days, new vulnerabilities
in these large scale, widely distributed
open source software.
And also recently with Cloud Mythos and Project Glasswing,
it's further demonstrated the power and capabilities
of frontier AI in cybersecurity capability.
And also, in our most recent work--
ExploitGym-- it also demonstrated
that frontier AI now not only that they can discover
vulnerabilities, discover previously
unknown vulnerabilities-- now also,
they have the capabilities to turn
the discovered vulnerabilities into exploits automatically,
and to generate exploits, to actually take malicious actions.
And furthermore, exploit image shows that the frontier AI
now not only that they can generate exploits,
but also they can actually generate exploit that can bypass
standard security mechanisms.
And also, I think many of you have heard recently the OpenAI
HuggingFace incident.
In that incident actually, OpenAI
is evaluating their agents actually
on our benchmark, ExploitGym.
So the agents were trying to solve the tasks on ExploitGym.
And unfortunately, in this case, the agents
was able to break out the isolation environment
and actually even HuggingFace infrastructure
to try to actually get information
from HuggingFace to help the agents to solve tasks
in ExploitGym.
So all this illustrates that now frontier AI model and agents
have really reached a level of capabilities that's
so powerful that the agents can autonomously actually attack
other well protected infrastructure.
And also this time, first, it shows
that evaluation infrastructure now is also
part of the attack surface.
And also the risk extends beyond the evaluation space.
So all this leads to that now we are at a critical point.
Frontier AI capabilities are advancing rapidly as our work
and others' work have shown.
And also, more concerning, the pace of progress
itself accelerating.
And also in addition, many researchers
also consider that recursive self-improvement, RSI,
plausible within the next few years, accelerating progress
in a way that could further outpace our ability
to understand and govern these systems.
So the key question here is how do we
ensure that agentic AI becomes one of humanity's greatest
advances while remaining safe, secure,
and beneficial for everyone?
And also, recently, we have seen various open letters
from Jensen, from Mark Zuckerberg,
from Demis, and so on.
And also, there is a recent pacing the frontier open letters
signed by over 1,000 leading AI researchers from frontier AI
labs--
including myself.
And also an open letter from leading economists as well.
So all these are calling essentially.
We are at a critical point.
We must act now.
And there are important questions
and also important questions to answer
and important decisions to make, what's the best
path for us to proceed?
So this is also where Berkeley RDI stands, and the mission
for Berkeley RDI.
So Berkeley RDI stands here to steward
the future of safe, secure, beneficial, agentic AI.
And the mission for Berkeley RDI is
to stewards the future of AI for human flourishing
by advancing the science, engineering,
and open ecosystem needed to ensure it is safe, secure,
and beneficial for everyone.
So Berkeley Center for Responsible Decentralized
Intelligence--
so let me quickly decipher the three words.
So responsible here means safe, secure, trustworthy.
And decentralized represents open ecosystem
beneficial to everyone.
And intelligence here, of course, is AI and agentic AI.
So in order to achieve this goal,
Bekeley RDI is a campus-wide multidisciplinary Innovation
Center.
It's one of only a very few number of research centers
that have been funded by the state of California.
And encompasses faculty and students
across campus from Berkeley, from CDSS--
where Jennifer is a dean-- and the School of Engineering,
has Business School and Law School.
And Berkeley RDI as an innovation center
has a unique structure.
We have three key pillars-- research, education, community
and entrepreneurship.
On the research front, we have three core commitments.
First, we focus on building safe and secure foundations,
develop science and engineering needed
for building safe, secure, trustworthy agentic AI.
Second, our core mission is to enable open ecosystem
to advance open frameworks, interoperable protocols,
and decentralized infrastructure,
so innovation and opportunities are broadly shared.
And the third one is guiding by measuring
what matters the most--
to create rigorous benchmarks, evaluations,
and scientific methods to measure capabilities, risks,
and societal impacts.
To help build the evidence base and guide
the future of agentic AI.
So with that, here are some quick examples
of some of the works that have been done in Berkeley RDI.
For building safe and secure foundations,
the researchers in RDI have built
advanced automated red teaming and defenses
for safe and secure agentic AI, developing broad spectrum
of different technologies and solutions.
And the work has won many best paper awards in top conferences
and so on.
And also, for enabling a future where frontier AI helps
defenders more attackers to build a secure foundation,
another example thrust the center has been focused on
is on building verifiable code generation
so that we can ensure that the AI-generated code is as secure.
For guiding by measuring what matters most, as some of you
may have seen, the benchmarks, for example,
have been developed and led by Berkeley RDI--
including cyber gym explosion, cyber gym end-to-end.
Many of these have been used by essentially our frontier AI
labs as a leading benchmark for measuring
frontier AI in cybersecurity.
And also, we have launched the frontier AI cybersecurity
observatory to help bring the community together
to continue to monitor the fast progress of frontier AI in cyber
capabilities.
And also, recently, we launched the Agents' Last Exam.
A new benchmark.
Aims at evaluating the agents performance on
real-world, economically valuable,
long horizon challenging tasks across a broad spectrum
of 55 different industry sectors,
covering over 90% of our digital domains.
And we welcome you to contribute further into this benchmark
as well.
And also, we recently launched the AgentBeats,
a new open framework for standardized reproducible agent
evaluation where we're actually identifying the agent
evaluation itself as well.
This is also in collaboration with many other institutions,
and we welcome everyone to participate here as well.
And also, Berkeley RDI has led efforts
on advancing science- and evidence-based AI
policy so that we can actually build the evidence
base to help provide needed information for AI policy.
And as I mentioned, guides the future of AI and agentic AI.
And the work has also served as a base for the report
to California Governor Newsom, and other legislation as well.
And so that's on the research side.
On the education side, Berkeley RDI has led a number of massive
open online courses, including the first MOOC on agentic AI
with over 40,000 enrolled globally,
and 14,000 on the discourse.
And Berkeley RDI YouTube channel has over 1 million views.
And also, Berkeley RDI has organized a global competitions
and hackathons with participants from over 1,000 universities
and colleges and over 1,000 companies as well.
And the hackathon competition together
have had around $2 million in prizes and resources.
And finally, for the entrepreneurship and community
pillar, Berkeley RDI also host the Berkeley Xcelerator,
which is a world-leading university-led accelerator.
And in the past, that has had seven cohorts
with 110 global teams, with follow on funding rates
over $650 million.
And today, on this stage, at 3:50 PM,
you can also watch this startup spotlight featuring this spring
cohort from Berkeley accelerator teams.
So with all this putting the three pillars together,
we hope that at Berkeley RDI as an innovation center.
As I mentioned, we can still voice
the safe, secure, beneficial future for agentic AI
that also enables human flourishing.
So this is also why we are convening this summit here.
As I mentioned, now we are at a critical point.
We hope that this summit can also
help gather the community together, share knowledge, build
an open ecosystem.
And together, we steward the future
of safe, secure, and beneficial agentic AI.
So with that, I welcome everyone at the summit.
We hope also you can help spread the word.
Please do help.
Join the social media tweets and posts about the summit.
And the summit is also a much larger scale than last year
as well.
We received close to 1,000 submissions for speaking
proposals and papers, and we have over 1,500 different
industry organizations represented here,
and over 250 different universities represented here,
with close to 5,000 in-person attendees.
And with that, I want to welcome everyone to the summit.
Please do enjoy.
We have four different stages, and also
a lounge for attendees at the Alumni House.
And a huge thanks to our sponsors and our community
partners.
So with that, I want to thank everyone and welcome everyone.
So please also help retweet and repost our tweet and LinkedIn
posts as well.
Thank you so much.
[APPLAUSE]
